findings.title: FastHenry's ratio-estimate feasibility (F1's 1 % cap) is checked on only one development pair, and FastHenry is the solver that missed it in P4
findings.detail: F7(c) measures the F1 exclusion rate on every Case 4 development pair, but only on l2_layout's ladder. FastHenry's three-level ratio estimate is checked only by F7(a), on 'one development pair' that the objective does not name. P4 found that FastHenry's trace-width ratio moved 0.66 % from k0 to k1, and its post-hoc check traced all of that step to the 4 mm plane pitch at k0. The objective does not fix FastHenry's plane-pitch ladder, so P4's own advice ('start at plane pitch <= 2 mm') is not binding. With a 4/2/1 mm plane ladder and a converged k2, gci_capped's lucky-grid branch gives 1.25|d1|/4: 0.21 % for P4's 2 mm edge move. It passes 1 % once the k0 artefact is about 5x larger, which is plausible for the large moves the span needs (r <= 0.75, three pairs below 0.90). Those pairs would then be excluded, A1 could not be met, and the run would end INCONCLUSIVE. This happens on exactly the large-effect pairs that carry coverage. A pass would still be correct; the risk is that the design cannot resolve the decision.
findings.evidence: research/o006_p4/results.json ratio_diff trace_width: R_fh k0 0.96299, k1 0.96956, k2 null, R_fh_est 0.0223. P4 note §3.4: k0 with 2 mm planes gives 0.96988 ('the plane pitch causes all of the k0 -> k1 change'). Scratch: gci_capped(0, d1, d1+1e-4) = 0.21 % at d1 = 0.66 %, 0.41 % at 2x, 0.62 % at 3x, 1.03 % at 5x.
findings.suggested_check: Before registration, have F7(a) (or a new F7 item) report FastHenry's three-level ratio estimate on the Case 4 development pairs with r <= 0.75 and on a trace-edge move, and fix FastHenry's coarsest plane pitch at <= 2 mm in the frozen ladder.

findings.title: The retry rule's direct-solver fallback cannot run at any level the judged solves use, so a cap of two retries makes crash-driven INVALID or INCONCLUSIVE likely
findings.detail: F1 retries a crash up to twice, 'FastHenry's direct solver where the multipole one crashes, D0002'. Direct LU needs about 8F^2 bytes (P4 §3.1 says it stops at about 15-20k filaments on 16 GB). That is about 84 GB at k1 (102k filaments), about 750 GB for the k1 thickness runs at nh 9 (about 306k), and about 1.36 TB at k2 (413k). So the fallback does not exist where it is needed, and the rule reduces to three multipole attempts. P4 measured 8 crashes in 32 attempts (25 %, Wilson 13-42 %). The crashes are SIGSEGVs 1-4 s into the run, not tied to the geometry, and cheap to retry. Assuming independent attempts, the chance that some finest-level run among about 15 layouts still lacks a value is about 21 % (range 3-68 %). That outcome is INVALID by F1. Across the roughly 75 FastHenry runs (3 lateral levels plus 2 thickness runs per layout), the chance is about 69 % (range 15-99.7 %). The objective does not say what a missing middle-level or thickness run means: excluded, or INVALID. The crash is value-independent, so no verdict is biased. But the stated fallback is factually unavailable, and the cap makes resolution unlikely within a $100 budget that has about 40 VM-hours per attempt.
findings.evidence: research/o006_p4/results.json n_filaments: k1 102192, k2 412584. P4 note §3.3: 8/32 crashes, all within 1-4 s, 'retrying works'. Scratch: 8F^2 = 83.5 GB, 749 GB, 1362 GB. P(3 crashes) = 0.0156 at p = 0.25; 1-(1-q)^15 = 0.21; 1-(1-q)^75 = 0.69.
findings.suggested_check: Replace the two-retry cap with unlimited (or about 10) retries of runs that crash before the preconditioner is formed, drop the direct-solver fallback above about 20k filaments, and define what a missing non-finest run means.

findings.title: Several model choices both solvers share are not listed in scope_out
findings.detail: The P4 exporter reads Layout.to_conductors(), the same conductor model l2_layout solves. It shares the trace lattice and leaves out gate and Kelvin wires, power-lead posts and die attach in both tools. Signal traces become floating conductors. scope_out lists only ideal die shorts, point-contact terminals, mitred polylines and lattice snapping, and F6 diagnoses only dies and terminal tabs. Agreement between the two solvers cannot detect these omissions.
findings.evidence: research/scripts/o006_p4/fh_export.py docstring line 41: 'not modelled (both): gate and Kelvin wires, power-lead posts, the ceramic (non-conductive), die attach as a conductor'. P4 note §1: 'the exporter reads only Layout.to_conductors(), the model l2_layout solves'.
findings.suggested_check: List every shared omission in scope_out so that the claim's scope names them.

findings.title: The covered 'ratio range' is not tied to a solver
findings.detail: decision_if_pass limits the pass to 'the ratio range the counted pairs cover', but the span is checked only on L1 at registration. If L1 overstates effects, the FastHenry or l2_layout span could be narrower. I checked that a constant-ratio predictor still fails A1 under plausible compression: 4.3 % even for a span of [0.90, 0.98]. So the null-predictor property holds; only the stated scope is ambiguous.
findings.suggested_check: State the covered range on FastHenry's finest ratios.

findings.title: The FastHenry binary differs from D0002's recorded hash
findings.detail: P4 ran a rebuilt binary (sha256 eaa6d6fc…), not D0002's 15bfbcd1…, and the burst VM will use a Linux build. D0002 pins the tarball and the build, not the binary. 'The pinned FastHenry build' should require recording the binary sha256 and passing the D0002 self-test on each VM.

findings.title: The FastHenry thickness ladder is not a ratio-2 refinement
findings.detail: With rh = 2, nh 3/5/9 gives surface filaments of about t/4, t/10 and t/46. gci_capped's docstring assumes r = 2. The estimate depends on the observed contraction rho, so it stays conservative if the sequence keeps contracting geometrically. It is a different use of the function from the one documented.
findings.evidence: research/o006_p4/results.json levels k0_nh5/k0_nh9: rh 2.0. Trace-width thickness ratio sequence 0.96299, 0.96713, 0.96921 gives gci_capped 0.26 %.

independent_checks_performed: Recomputed F8's constant-ratio bound: the best constant on [0.75, 0.98] errs by 13.3 %. It still fails A1 at 10.1 %, 7.1 % and 4.3 % if FastHenry's span is compressed to a lower end of 0.80, 0.85 or 0.90. A1 cannot be met by a predictor that ignores the geometry.
Recomputed the clustered bounds: 1 - 0.05^(1/13) = 20.6 % and 1 - 0.05^(1/2) = 77.6 %, as stated.
Ran mfos.metrics.gci_capped on P3's l2_layout ladders (1.0/0.5/0.25 mm): base 0.99 %, trace_width 0.96 %, die_shift 1.02 % of L. This confirms K2's 'about 1 % lateral' rationale.

Tested the 'steps below 0.1 % count as converged' rule on P3's divergent trace-width ratio sequence (steps 0.0073 %, 0.0252 %; gci_capped gives +inf). The rule gives 3 max|d| = 0.076 %. Extrapolating each L by Richardson and dividing moves the ratio by 0.033 %, so the rule bounds it.
Checked the claimed P4 absolute agreement of 0.8-2.5 % against the P4 table and results.json: confirmed.
Computed FastHenry's gci_capped behaviour with P4's k0 plane-pitch artefact under the lucky-grid branch: 0.21 % at the observed d1, and about 1 % at 5x.
Computed direct-LU memory (8F^2) at P4's filament counts: about 84 GB at k1, about 750 GB for the k1 nh 9 thickness runs, about 1.36 TB at k2.

Computed the probability that a run lacks a value under the two-retry cap from P4's 8/32 crash rate and its Wilson interval: about 21 % for the finest runs alone and about 69 % across all FastHenry runs, at the central rate.
Computed skin depths: Cu 20.9 / 14.8 µm and Al 25.9 / 18.3 µm at 10 / 20 MHz. Both frequencies are in the high-frequency regime (P3: L differs by 0.6 % and ratios by about 0.01 % between them).

Checked the size of the round-versus-square wire term (T0364): the equal-GMD square side 0.8711 d, with its 2D equivalent radius of 0.5902 side, gives ln(0.514/0.5) = 2.8 % of the log term, about 0.6-0.8 % of a wire's partial self-inductance. Consistent with the stated 0.6 %.
Read the P4 exporter's model table and docstring to see which model choices the two solvers share.
caveats: The pass statement follows from A1, A2 and F1 as written. A1 met means every pair was counted, FastHenry's ratio estimate is <= 1 % and the raw difference is <= 2 %. That establishes ratio agreement within 2 % plus FastHenry's estimate, but only against FastHenry, which shares the conductor model, the lattice and the leaving-out of gate/Kelvin wires and power-lead posts. It is not agreement with the real module.

Whether the design can resolve the decision depends on F7. The FastHenry exclusion risk on large-effect pairs and the crash-driven INVALID risk under the two-retry cap should be fixed before registration, or the run will probably end INCONCLUSIVE or INVALID for reasons unrelated to the solvers' values.
K1 and K2 can fire on raw values whatever the exclusions. Their only escape is the value-independent INVALID for a missing finest solve, which is why the crash cap matters.
10 and 20 MHz are both deep in the high-frequency regime and give nearly identical ratios, so 'both frequencies' adds no independent evidence.
Physics lens only; the statistical clustering of the 13 pairs was checked arithmetically, not judged.
